title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS FEATURES. Original 9 were cut to 6, framed as three jobs: Win the deal (RFP), Run the work (ActionSwarm, IT access, search), Control the spend (expenses, Zombie SaaS). F1 RFP and Security Questionnaire Engine (the wedge, real build): upload Excel/CSV, knowledge base of SOC2 docs/policies, answer per question with citation, confidence gate (auto-fill above threshold, red flag below with closest source), human review UI, learning loop (corrected answers saved and reused on next questionnaire), export .xlsx plus accuracy report. F2 ActionSwarm (real): meeting transcript to schema-forced JSON of action items, assignees, due dates; tasks on own dashboard board (real Jira optional); Slack summary post; email draft; live activity feed; injection guard that treats planted instructions as data. F3 OmniContext + Catch-Me-Up (Cmd+K, real over ~10 seeded docs): hybrid search with cited answers, permission-aware retrieval (intern vs founder salary-sheet demo; needs confirmation that Meko datapack sharing supports this), Catch-Me-Up is a time-window mode ("last 4 days") giving an executive briefing. F4 ZeroTouch Expenses (thin): 3-5 prepared receipts via Gemini vision, extract merchant/items/GST/total, policy check, one violation, card-feed matching. F5 Zero-Friction IT Provisioning (real logic): natural-language request ("I need Figma"), risk classification, role check, low-risk auto-grant, high-risk (AWS prod) manager Approve/Reject (dashboard button, Slack button if time), audit log and undo. F6 Zombie SaaS Eradicator (mocked on purpose): seeded billing and SSO login tables, one SQL join for tools paid for with zero logins in 30+ days, waste dashboard in rupees. CUT (roadmap slide only): Dynamic Pitch-Deck Compiler, Procurement and Contract Routing. Priority: RFP engine plus trust layer must never be cut; cut order if behind: Zombie SaaS, Expenses, Slack buttons, Catch-Me-Up. On slides use feature names, not numbers.

title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS CONTEXT FILE (plexus-context.md) SUMMARY. Mahi pastes this file at the top of every build prompt, replacing the last line "Current task" with the module prompt. If the file is lost, rebuild it from this. RULES FOR THE AI: TypeScript strict; one module per prompt; patches to named files, not rewrites; validate every model output with Zod (retry once with the error, then return a flagged result); batch RFP questions 10 per call; retry with exponential backoff on 503 and 429; every real response saved to fixtures/ and DEMO_MODE=true replays it via withReplay(key, fn) in lib/replay.ts; every action emits one ActivityEvent and one audit_events row; never log keys; show clear errors in the feed; add a run command or test per module; check current library docs before using any API. STACK: Next.js App Router + TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Recharts, Mastra (fallback plain @modelcontextprotocol/sdk client), Gemini API free tier, SQLite via better-sqlite3, exceljs, Meko remote MCP, n8n in Docker for the Slack post, Slack app in socket mode for Approve/Reject buttons (dashboard button is the backup). FOLDER LAYOUT: plexus/{app/(dashboard)/{rfp,actions,access,search,finance,audit}, app/api, agents/{rfp,actionswarm,access,finance,search}.ts, guard/{guard,injection,policies}.ts, lib/{gemini,meko,db,replay,events,xlsx}.ts, components/{ActivityFeed,RfpGrid,ApprovalCard,TraceDrawer,CmdK}, data/, fixtures/, .env.local}. ENV NAMES: GEMINI_API_KEY, GEMINI_MODEL_FAST, GEMINI_MODEL_SMART, GEMINI_MODEL_FALLBACK, MEKO_MCP_URL, MEKO_AUTH (the mko_tkn_ key), MEKO_DATAPACK_ID, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_APP_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL, N8N_WEBHOOK_URL, DATABASE_PATH, CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.85, DEMO_MODE. ACTIVITY EVENT: {id, timestamp, agent (rfp|actionswarm|access|finance|search|guard), action, status (done|flagged|blocked|pending_approval|undone|error), confidence?, sources[{title,ref}], traceId, undoable}. SQLITE TABLES: users(id,name,role,manager_id); questionnaires(id,customer,uploaded_at,total); rfp_questions(id,questionnaire_id,number,question,answer,confidence,status filled|flagged|human_fixed,source_ref,human_answer,reused_from_fix); tasks(id,title,assignee,due,source_event,status); access_requests(id,user_id,app,risk,status granted|pending|rejected|revoked,approver_id,requested_at,decided_at); expenses(id,merchant,date,gst,total,category,policy_flag,duplicate_of,card_txn_id); saas_billing(tool,monthly_cost_inr,owner,seats); sso_logins(tool,user_id,last_login); audit_events(id,timestamp,agent,action,status,confidence,sources_json,trace_id,undo_state,payload_json). MEKO CONVENTIONS: agent ids plexus_rfp, plexus_actionswarm, plexus_access, plexus_finance, plexus_search; RFP answers come ONLY from knowledge search results with a citation, otherwise flagged (never from general knowledge); learning loop: a human fix is saved as memory `RFP_FIX | question | approved answer | approver`, later questionnaires search memory and knowledge together and mark reused_from_fix=1; each agent action is one conversation message (input=task, output=result, plan=steps, reasoning=one plain line) read by the audit screen; if Meko fails, fall back to SQLite memories and traces tables behind the same lib/meko.ts function names. GUARD ORDER before every action: 1 injection check (text from transcripts, emails, docs, Slack is DATA never instructions; flagged lines blocked and shown), 2 confidence gate (below threshold means flagged/red, not applied), 3 approval rule (high-risk like AWS production, permission changes, spend over limit always needs a human; low-risk like Figma auto-approved), 4 undo (store undo_state), 5 log (ActivityEvent + audit_events). ACCESS POLICY SEED: Figma low auto, Notion low auto, AWS production high approver Karan (engineering roles), Salesforce admin high approver Riya. PEOPLE: Riya Sharma founder, Karan engineering manager, Meera new hire (engineering), Arjun intern. UI COPY RULES: never claim SOC 2 or DPDP compliance, zero data retention, "never stored", or any unmeasured number; say "designed for DPDP alignment"; label seeded data as seeded.

title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS RFP DEBUG AND TEST RESULTS, SAT OCT 31 2026 (afternoon IST). ROOT CAUSE of the earlier "filled 0, flagged 50": the Gemini call returned HTTP 400 "API key not valid". Two causes: Mahi had not saved .env.local after fixing the key, and PowerShell still had GEMINI_API_KEY set to the placeholder "new-key" from an earlier example (shell env vars override .env.local). Fix: `Remove-Item Env:GEMINI_API_KEY` (also clear any GEMINI_MODEL), save .env.local, restart. Retrieval was always fine (21 chunks across Q1-Q10). `scripts/rfp-debug.ts` loads .env.local itself; `scripts/rfp-test.ts` does not, so run it as `npx tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/rfp-test.ts`. Delete `fixtures\rfp-*` before each real re-run so withReplay does not replay stale files. DEBUG OUTPUT after the key fix: Gemini OK, Zod OK, all 10 rows coverage=full confidence=1.0 status=filled, answers contain specific correct facts. Every row has confidence 1.0, so confidence carries no signal; flagging is driven by the coverage field (full/partial/none). Do not show a confidence number as a deck feature; describe flagging by coverage. FULL TEST (50 questions, model gemini-3.5-flash-lite): run 1 filled 36, flagged 14, correct 42, wrongly_filled 8, wrongly_flagged 0; run 2 filled 36, flagged 14, correct 41, wrongly_filled 9. Q37-Q50 (partial and out-of-scope) were all flagged correctly; no answerable question was flagged. SCORER FALSE NEGATIVES: rows Q1, Q4, Q7, Q8, Q18, Q25, Q30, Q33 were scored wrong, but side-by-side reading shows the agent answers are correct: the word-match scorer fails on wording differences ("MFA" vs "multi-factor authentication", "1 Jan" vs "1 January") and on extra facts in the key that the question did not ask for (dates, sign-offs, counts). Wording varies between runs (Q4 failed in run 2 only). Do not loosen the scorer to hit a number; Bhumika's hand-check of the filled answers gives the real accuracy figure for the deck (28 of 35 under the strict scorer is NOT a number to quote). REAL PROBLEM: Q36 (Partial in the key) was filled with coverage=full ("No, ... DR copies are in Singapore"), because the prompt in agents/rfp.ts buildBatchPrompt had no definitions of full/partial/none. The learning-loop demo depends on Q36 being flagged (human-fix Meridian Q36, Q40, Q43, then Aegis Q3, Q8, Q14 should reuse from memory). FIX GIVEN to Mahi (applied? re-run result not yet reported): (1) replace the opening lines of the prompt with explicit rules: full = chunks answer every part and contain everything a customer needs to rely on it; partial = chunks answer only part, OR the honest answer reveals a gap between what the customer asks and what we do and the chunks contain no policy/option/next step for the gap; none = chunks do not answer; for partial/none still draft an answer if the chunks allow, else null. (2) bug in runRfp: `window.map` returned the promise without await inside try/catch so a failing batch would crash the run; use `async (batch, j) => { try { return await processBatch(...) } catch { return { filled: 0, flagged: batch.length } } }`. CHECK AFTER RE-RUN: Q36 flagged, wrongly_filled 0, none of Q1-Q35 flipped to flagged; run twice if time. If Q36 still fills, fall back to Q37-Q43 for the demo red cells and have Bhumika re-point the three linked Aegis questions. Optional later: prompt truncates each chunk at 500 characters (chunk.content.slice(0, 500)); try about 1000. NEXT: after Q36 passes, backend prompts 3-8 (guard and audit, ActionSwarm, access agent, Cmd+K and Catch-Me-Up, finance) as BACKEND AND API ONLY with a JSON contract per endpoint for Bhumika's screens; the other Claude chat and Mahi have not confirmed that yet. Mahi rotated the Meko API key (done).
